target_paper.title: Cultural bias and cultural alignment of large language models
target_paper.original_source: OSF wide tables / coordinates_on_map for gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and PNAS Nexus Datasets S5-S6, re-scored with the projection recovered from the released tables (residual 5e-14)

generation.parameters: temperature 0, max_tokens 256, top_p 1 (Part1/Part2 generation pipelines); district names passed with underscores as the authors did
generation.battery: 10 questions x 10 descriptor variants x (1 default + 107 districts) = 10,800 calls, 1 pass

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN §1; human double-coding pending
results.note: Cultural prompting reduces the mean distance by 0.933 (CI95 [0.711, 1.14]) vs 0.934 [0.707, 1.138] originally; 78.5% of countries improve (81.3% originally); Wilcoxon p 5e-11. The default position drifted slightly toward the origin (2.523 vs 2.706 mean distance) but stays in the English-speaking / Protestant-Europe region. 87% of the 10,200 answer cells are identical to the 2024 archive at temperature 0.

reproducibility_frictions_observed: IVS microdata (WVS/EVS) is registration-only and absent from OSF; the map projection was recovered as an affine map from the released wide tables and country coordinates, reproducing Datasets S5-S6 exactly

the Results text's closest/farthest countries (Netherlands 0.21, Switzerland 0.28, Iceland 0.31; Jordan 4.34) do not match the paper's own Dataset S5 (New Zealand 0.125, Australia 0.323, Iceland 0.381; Jordan 4.195); the card's original values were re-based on Dataset S5
6 of 107 districts have no raw response file on OSF (wide tables cover them)
same dated snapshot served by 10 backend fingerprints; 13% of cells changed at temperature 0
